html:
The Menologion of Basil II is a Byzantine illuminated manuscript made around 1000 for Emperor Basil II. It is a church calendar, giving short lives of the saints and the feasts to be kept on each day, for the half of the year from September to February.

Most entries have a painting beside the text, about 430 in all, in bright colour on gold. Many show the deaths of martyrs, set among churches, landscapes and Bible scenes. Unusually, the names of eight painters are written in the margins, so this is one of the few Byzantine works where we know who made the pictures.

It is one of the richest works of the Macedonian Renaissance, made in Constantinople at the height of Basil's power. It later reached Italy and is now in the Vatican Library in Rome.
